core_obligations: Choose generators of the two given finite modules and lift them to elements of the fibre product, verifying that the lifts of the second family generate the second module (proof lines 782-793).
Claim that the two families together generate the fibre product and take an arbitrary element of it (proof lines 793-797).
Correct the element in the first component by the lifts of the first family, using surjectivity of the ring map (proof lines 797-800).

Write the remaining difference in the ideal times the second module, lift the coefficients to the fibre product and conclude that the original element lies in the submodule generated by the two families (proof lines 800-803).
proof_roadmap: Lift generators to the fibre product (proof lines 782-793).
Reduce an arbitrary element to one vanishing in the first component (proof lines 793-800).
Use the ideal and the lifted coefficients to conclude generation (proof lines 800-804).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the fibre product of two finite modules over a fibre product of rings is again finite, and the proof is a 23-line generation argument. It chooses generators of the two modules, lifts them to elements of the fibre product using the identifications of the two base changes with the outer modules, shows that the images of the second family of lifts generate the second module, and then verifies by an explicit computation that the two families together generate the fibre product: an arbitrary element is first corrected in the first component and the resulting difference is written in the ideal times the second module, whose coefficients are then lifted through the kernel of the surjection of rings. The generation claim and the correction step are the content, and both are displayed.
